status_note: Narrower than recorded, still open on main (a4d8e00342d0): the test cases expect IEEE `±inf` on overflow with the default options (`multiply.test` L19-L21, likewise `add`, `subtract`, `divide`, `sum`, `exp`, since [#738](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/pull/738)), but no fp implementation offers raising instead ([`functions_arithmetic.yaml` L45-L62](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_arithmetic.yaml#L45-L62), [`functions_arithmetic.yaml` L401-L412](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_arithmetic.yaml#L401-L412), [`functions_arithmetic.yaml` L445-L468](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_arithmetic.yaml#L445-L468)), and `sum`'s `overflow` values ([`functions_arithmetic.yaml` L1092-L1111](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/blob/a4d8e00342d0/extensions/functions_arithmetic.yaml#L1092-L1111)) are undefined for floats. No existing issue; [#254](https://github.com/substrait-io/substrait/issues/254) (options undocumented).
summary: The `fp32` and `fp64` implementations of `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `power`, `exp` and the other elementary functions have no option for a result too large for the type: only `rounding` (and `on_domain_error`, `on_division_by_zero` where they apply). The test cases expect IEEE 754's `±inf` with the default options (`multiply.test`, since substrait#738), but nothing lets a plan ask for an error instead. `sum` and `avg` of `fp64` take `overflow: SILENT | SATURATE | ERROR`, which the YAML defines for integers only.
repro: DuckDB 2.0 gives `inf` for all of them (fact duckdb-double-overflow); Polars gives `inf` (fact polars-double-arith); sverify's reference raises (#575).
handling: The reference raises when an operation on finite doubles gives `±inf` (`Issue.infinite`): an inferred precondition the written plan checks on the data, as for a `SUM` that leaves 64 bits. The core allows both behaviours.

Could be expressed as: an `overflow` option on the floating-point implementations, with `IEEE` (`±inf`) and `ERROR`, and the meaning of `sum`'s existing `overflow` values stated for `fp32` and `fp64` (`SATURATE` to the largest finite value).
found_by: the terminology of the loose core (#574), docs/core-semantics.md
